completeness.label: Completeness
completeness.detail: The seven key fields are patient, age/sex, date, hospital, doctor, diagnosis and vitals. A field counts as found when it's filled in and not marked ‘Not specified’.

confidence.label: Reading confidence
confidence.formula: how sure the engine is it read the script correctly
confidence.detail: Starts higher for typed/printed scripts than for handwritten ones, goes up the more complete the script is, and drops for every field the engine couldn't read cleanly. Shown on a 60–99 scale.

review.label: Auto-clear vs review
review.formula: send to a human if anything was unclear or a field is missing
review.detail: If every field was read cleanly and nothing is missing, the script passes straight through. A single illegible or missing field sends it to a person to check — the engine never guesses.

case.label: Case type
case.detail: Emergency or admission wording → acute/emergency. A long-term condition in the diagnosis (e.g. diabetes, hypertension, cancer) → chronic. Otherwise judged by how long the medicines run: 90+ days chronic, 15–89 sub-acute, under 15 acute.

refill.label: Refill candidate
refill.formula: any medicine runs a month or longer
refill.detail: Flags scripts where the patient is on ongoing medication, so they're a good fit for a refill or subscription reminder.

poly.label: Multiple medicines (5+)
poly.detail: Counts only actual medicines (tests and supportive-care items don't count). These patients are candidates for an adherence pack.

diagnostics.label: Lab-test opportunity
diagnostics.formula: a test is ordered or a lab value is recorded
diagnostics.detail: Flags scripts that either order a diagnostic test or note a lab/vital reading — a natural fit for a diagnostics offer.

therapeutic_class.label: Types of therapy
therapeutic_class.formula: medicines grouped by what they treat
therapeutic_class.detail: Medicines are grouped into therapy types (for example antibiotics, painkillers, chronic-care) so you can see what the scripts are mostly for.

category_split.label: What's on the scripts
category_split.detail: Each line on a prescription is one of three kinds — a medicine, a diagnostic test, or supportive care. This is the mix across all lines in the set.

specialty.label: Medical specialties
specialty.detail: Each script is tagged with the medical area it came from (for example cardiology, dermatology) to show which specialties are represented.
